PRODUCT ORACLE V2, WAVE 2 (API AND LOGIC), LANE v2-specs. You are one of several lanes building Product Oracle v2 in parallel, each in its own SwarmCloud task and PR. Wave 1 is merged in your checkout: the foundation (oracle/v2/ schemas, artifact tables, oracle/changes.py, oracle/readiness.py), modules, blockers, intake, trace, review and quality. Build on them.

Read first, in this order:
1. docs/product-oracle-v2/build-prompt.md, the owner's build prompt: §0-§3, §12, §14, §15 and §16 in full, then your sections (§11.1, §11.2, §11.5).
2. docs/product-oracle-v2/waves.md: the plan, the hooks and the shared rules. Follow its shared rules exactly. The next free migration number is in its merge notes.
3. docs/questions.md: owner decisions, which take precedence. Where your work would conflict with one, build the compatible version and add a row to docs/product-oracle-v2/change-requests.md.
4. docs/product-oracle-v2/01-solution-architecture.md, 05-artifact-contracts.md and docs/build-brief.md, then the code you extend.

NO UI IN THIS LANE (I3 UI visual language, owner 2026-10-19: the UI is redesigned first). Build the API, the logic, OpenAPI and MCP tools, and mock API fixtures. Do not change web/app or web/components. In your report, list every screen your feature needs, with its states, data and actions.

YOUR SCOPE: CR-09, engineering specs, flows and low-fidelity wireframes, linked to the approved PRD.
1. A technical brief per feature, and optionally a full engineering spec, with every section §11.1 lists. These are Oracle documents (a new document kind), with brief and full layers, versions and review like PRDs. They keep "product requirement" (from the approved PRD, by requirement id) visibly apart from "proposed engineering approach", which is not decided until an engineering approver approves it. Without a code capability map, assumptions are labelled as such.
2. Per O2: SVG flow diagrams and grayscale low-fidelity HTML wireframes for 2-4 key screens chosen from approved requirements, each linked to the exact section and requirement ids. Annotations are reviewable. Generated HTML is static, sanitised, and has no scripts or network.
3. Generation runs through the existing runs framework as a new code-defined flow from an approved PRD version (like prd_to_roadmap), with the >$50 approval and >1.5x pause intact. Agents return candidate artifacts, which Oracle validates (names, sizes, types) and stores as artifact versions with provenance: PRD version, requirement ids, run, runner and prompt version. Tests use the fake runtime.
4. Lineage and staleness: every spec, flow and wireframe registers artifact dependencies. A change to its PRD section or requirement marks it potentially_stale through oracle/changes.py. It is never rewritten automatically; regeneration is a proposed task.
5. Tests: §16 item 19, and item 20 for the wireframe HTML (no scripts, no network).

Finish: commit on your branch (tests first, then code), run everything the shared rules list, and write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/v2-specs-report.md as waves.md describes.

YOUR SCOPE: CR-11, roadmap and engineering alignment, by extending prd_to_roadmap and the five roadmap templates. Do not replace them.
1. Each roadmap item traces to the exact approved PRD version, feature and requirement ids, through the trace lane's links. Add blocker dependencies (from oracle/blockers), validation gates, economics, and drift from engineering status where known.
2. Now/Next/Later and the planning horizons stay the default (O4). A dated milestone is allowed only with verified estimates, capacity or commitments recorded against it. Never invent dates; test that a date without a verified basis is refused.
3. Tracker alignment: a read-only alignment report (roadmap against tracker state) is the path that works without write permission. A two-way Linear/Jira connector stays behind a disabled gate, with no unattended external writes.
4. Brief and full views, themed decks and exports, and the roadmap_review approval loop keep working.
5. A changed PRD requirement marks the roadmap items tracing to it potentially_stale (oracle/changes.py).
6. Tests: §16 item 18 and staleness of roadmap items.
7. Product tracks (V2b in docs/questions.md): an accepted (published) PRD starts a product track. A track has its roadmap, milestones and items traced to the PRD. Oracle monitors each track: status, drift from plan (engineering status where known, read-only), the next milestone, and items at risk (blocked, stale or slipping), with change events through oracle/changes.py. Routes for tracks and their monitoring, shaped for one calm overview per track. Background derivation and monitoring runs in SwarmCloud (V2c, V2d), never on Oracle's own model configuration.

Finish: commit on your branch (tests first, then code), run everything the shared rules list, and write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/v2-roadmap-report.md as waves.md describes.

YOUR SCOPE: CR-13, the Head of Product chat backend and review notifications.
FIRST: decision I4 in docs/questions.md chose a workspace over a chat-first app, and the chat was deferred. Add a change-requests.md row: the build prompt asks for a contextual chat PANEL inside the workspace, not a chat-first app. Build it on that basis.
1. A contextual chat about the current document, version and section, on the existing built-in model jobs (docs/llm-jobs.md), not SwarmCloud. It can:
   - answer questions about the document;
   - explain priorities, constraints and blockers from Oracle's data;
   - turn a conversation into explicit structured feedback or suggested edits, which become review feedback and targeted patch proposals through the review lane;
   - respectfully challenge an unsupported decision, citing evidence ids.
   It never publishes, never edits locked or approved sections, and never accepts its own suggestions. Conversations are company-scoped and audited. Ingested content is data, never instructions.
2. Review notifications: in-app notifications for assignments, due dates, comments and approvals requested. Slack delivery stays behind a disabled gate, using the existing Slack connection; it is an external write, so it is off by default and needs an owner-enabled setting.
3. Routes for chat threads, messages and conversion to feedback, plus notifications. Every route is role-guarded and company-scoped, with negative cross-company tests.
4. Tests: chat never mutates a locked section; conversion produces reviewable proposals; notifications respect roles; Slack is off unless enabled.

Finish: commit on your branch (tests first, then code), run everything the shared rules list, and write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/v2-chat-report.md as waves.md describes.

YOUR SCOPE: CR-12, source freshness, ACL and code understanding, by extending sources/ and connections/.
1. Freshness: incremental sync where a connector supports it (webhooks only where an existing connection can verify them). "New evidence since version X" for a document version, read from the snapshots. The intake lane's snapshot lock stays authoritative for in-progress work.
2. ACL metadata: keep each source item's permission metadata from its connector, and prepare per-user source access mirroring (store and evaluate, no enforcement change for the current internal policy) as the gate before external sale. A source revoked after a run was queued cannot be retrieved afterwards: test it.
3. Public-link hardening: verify and test SSRF defences (private and metadata ranges, redirects, DNS rebinding), decompression bombs and hostile MIME types. Fix gaps.
4. The code capability map: an indexer for connected GitHub repositories that maps modules, routes and capabilities, behind a disabled gate, stored as source items with provenance. Specs use it when present.
5. Never ingest Slack DMs. Connector credentials never reach an LLM, a prompt or a log.
6. Tests: revocation after queueing, SSRF cases, ACL metadata round-trip, and §16 item 12 for source routes.

Finish: commit on your branch (tests first, then code), run everything the shared rules list, and write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/v2-sources-report.md as waves.md describes.

YOUR SCOPE: CR-14, operational resilience and costs across the new flows.
1. Cost per run and per phase, projected and actual. The >$50 owner approval and the >1.5x pause after the current segment are preserved for every new flow (specs, roadmap, intake research). Test them.
2. Run provenance: source snapshot, prompt, tool and runner versions, cost, status, reviewer actions and the final artifact version, with no secrets (§16 item 24).
3. Duplicate-dispatch protection for the new flows: a submit timeout followed by a retry never creates two accepted proposals or a silent double charge, and reconciliation is observable (§16 item 15). Reuse the adapter's label de-duplication. Do not change the adapter's protocol.
4. Status semantics everywhere: unavailable, blocked, failed, retryable, partial and succeeded. Cancel and resume are visible and idempotent. A missing result is never a successful draft.
5. Audit events for run dispatch and spend.
6. Tests for each of the above, with the fake runtime.
7. V2c and V2d (docs/questions.md): move every BACKGROUND built-in model job to SwarmCloud tasks through the runs framework and adapter: classifying and de-duplicating requests and feedback, readiness evaluation, reports, research. Keep on Oracle's own model configuration only what a person waits for: interviews, the Head of Product chat, and click-and-wait actions (refine this section, review this section, suggest a rewrite). List every current job type in your report with where it now runs, and test that a background job no longer touches the local pool.

Finish: commit on your branch (tests first, then code), run everything the shared rules list, and write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/v2-ops-report.md as waves.md describes.

YOUR SCOPE: requests and feedback in one inbox (V2b in docs/questions.md).
1. One model for feature requests and feedback from every source: connected sources (support, sales notes, Slack public channels, Notion, GitHub issues), people in Oracle, review comments, and interviews (team and customer, from the interviews lane). Each request keeps its source links and evidence, its requester (unverified when it came from a customer interview), and its company scoping.
2. Classification and de-duplication run in SwarmCloud as background work (V2c and V2d), as proposals: merge duplicates, link to goals and features in the baseline, suggest qualified or disqualified. A person with the right role qualifies or disqualifies each request with a reason; the decision is audited and reversible.
3. Qualified requests feed the baseline (proposals), intake (a request can start a new product idea) and priorities. Disqualified ones stay searchable with their reason.
4. During PRD review, review suggestions and feedback are qualified or disqualified the same way (accept, or reject with a reason), through the review lane's feedback items. Extend them; do not duplicate them.
5. Routes for the inbox, merging, linking, qualify and disqualify. Every route role-guarded and company-scoped, with negative cross-company tests.
6. Tests: a duplicate merge keeps both sources; disqualifying needs a reason; a request from a customer interview is marked unverified.

Finish: commit on your branch (tests first, then code), run everything the shared rules list, and write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/v2-requests-report.md as waves.md describes.

2. docs/product-oracle-v2/waves.md: the plan, the hooks and the shared rules. Follow its shared rules exactly. The next free migration number is in its merge notes.

YOUR SCOPE: interactive interviews instead of forms (V2b, V2d and V2e in docs/questions.md).
1. A team-member interview: the intake's questions (and review questions) asked as a real-time conversation with Oracle, which follows up, accepts "I don't know", defer, ask someone and research this, and writes the answers into the intake's question and answer ledger and gaps. It is real-time, so it runs on Oracle's own model configuration (V2d), never SwarmCloud. Streaming responses where the existing LLM transport allows it.
2. A customer interview (V2e): a team member creates a private invite per customer: a single-use link that expires after 7 days and opens ONLY that interview, with no account and no other access to Oracle. The link carries a high-entropy token stored hashed. It is revocable and rate-limited, and is never logged or put in URLs that reach third parties. The customer types answers; Oracle asks and follows up. Answers land in Requests (the requests lane's model) as customer-interview evidence, with the customer's name as given and marked unverified.
3. Safety: the interview prompt treats everything the customer types as data, never as instructions. The customer sees no company data beyond the interview's own questions; test a prompt-injection attempt and an attempt to read other data. Company and customer data never reach SwarmCloud prompts from this path.
4. Routes for interviews, invites (create, revoke, list), the public interview endpoint (token-only, no other auth), and the transcript. Everything is audited.
5. Tests: invite single use and expiry, revocation, the token stored hashed, no cross-company access, the injection attempt refused, answers landing in the ledger and in Requests.

Finish: commit on your branch (tests first, then code), run everything the shared rules list, and write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/v2-interviews-report.md as waves.md describes.
